claim: AWS Shield Advanced costs a monthly fee of $3,000 per month per organization, plus Shield Advanced data transfer usage fees for the resources it protects.

evidence.quote: With AWS Shield Advanced, you pay a monthly fee of $3,000 per month per organization. In addition, you also pay for AWS Shield Advanced Data Transfer usage fees for AWS resources enabled for advanced protection.

claim: AWS Shield Advanced requires a 1-year subscription commitment and a monthly fee, plus a usage fee based on data transfer out from CloudFront, ELB, EC2 and Global Accelerator; subscriptions auto-renew annually.
question: What commitment term does an AWS Shield Advanced subscription require?

qualifiers.condition: all Shield Advanced benefits, including DDoS cost protection, are subject to fulfilling the 1-year commitment

claim: With Shield Advanced you pay one monthly subscription fee for all accounts created under a consolidated billing account, plus usage fees based on GB of data transferred out.
question: Does each account in an organization pay its own Shield Advanced fee?

qualifiers.condition: the organization must own all of the accounts and their resources; channel resellers are billed differently

evidence.quote: With Shield Advanced, you pay one monthly subscription fee for all accounts created under a consolidated billing account, plus usage fees based on GB of data transferred out.
You will pay the monthly fee once as long as your payer account owns the AWS accounts and resources in those accounts that are linked to it.

claim: In the AWS Shield pricing examples, Shield Advanced data transfer out usage fees are $0.050 per GB for an Application Load Balancer and $0.025 per GB for a CloudFront distribution.

qualifiers.scope: per GB of data transfer out from protected resources
qualifiers.condition: example rates from the pricing page; if CloudFront sits in front of the ELB and receives all its traffic, you only need to protect CloudFront

evidence.quote: In addition to the monthly fee you will be charged $50 on the 1,000 GB of Regional Data Transfer out at $0.050 per GB (as AWS Shield Data Transfer Out usage fees).

claim: A Shield Advanced subscription includes standard AWS WAF fees (web ACLs, rules and request fees for web ACLs within the default 1,500 WCUs) for Shield-protected resources, for up to 50 billion AWS WAF requests per month.
question: Which AWS WAF costs does a Shield Advanced subscription cover?

qualifiers.scope: per subscribed payer ID, per calendar month
qualifiers.condition: requests that Shield Advanced detects as DDoS do not count towards the 50 billion; requests beyond it are billed

evidence.quote: The Shield Advanced subscription includes certain AWS WAF usage for Shield protected resources at no additional cost for up to 50 billion AWS WAF requests per month. This includes the monthly fees for WebACLs, rules, and request fees for WebACLs with default (1,500) WCU limits.
As part of your subscription, you will get up to 50 billion requests per subscribed payer ID to AWS Shield protected WAF resources in a calendar month.

note: The Shield FAQ says customers 'will now be limited to 50B AWS WAF requests per month' with the L7 DDoS feature; no dated change row gives the start date.

claim: Shield Advanced does not cover AWS WAF for resources that it does not protect, nor non-standard WAF costs such as Bot Control, the CAPTCHA action, web ACLs above 1,500 WCUs, and body inspection beyond the default size.
question: Which AWS WAF costs are not covered by Shield Advanced?

evidence.quote: Your subscription to Shield Advanced does not cover the use of AWS WAF for resources that you do not protect using Shield Advanced. It also does not cover any additional non-standard AWS WAF costs for protected resources. Examples of non-standard AWS WAF costs are those for Bot Control, for the CAPTCHA rule action, for web ACLs that use more than 1,500 WCUs, and for inspecting the request body beyond the default body size.

evidence.quote: Enabling Shield Advanced automatic application layer DDoS mitigation adds a rule group to your protection pack (web ACL) that uses 150 web ACL capacity units (WCUs). These WCUs count against the WCU usage in your protection pack (web ACL).
